`weave.init()` sets up Weave tracing for your Python script and ties it to a team and project. Pass a string like `"your-team/your-project"`.

- **What it does:** It registers your team and project so the SDK routes spans to the correct place in the UI [S1]. In the agent quickstart, it also authenticates with Weights & Biases and configures the OTel exporter that sends agent spans to the Agents view. If the project doesn't exist on your team, Weave creates it the first time you write to it [S2]. For agent tracing, call it before `start_conversation()`, `start_turn()` and similar calls. Those functions silently do nothing when tracing is disabled or the init call is absent [S1].
- **What to pass:** Use `"[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]"`. The team is your CoreWeave Forge team name and the project is your Weights & Biases project name [S1]. In the OpenAI integration guide, if you don't specify a team, Weave uses your default entity [S3].

```python
import weave

weave.init("my-team/my-project")  # placeholders: use your own team and project
```

Caveat: I didn't find a Python API reference page for `weave.init` in this snapshot. These details come from the guides, so they aren't a full parameter list. The quickstart sets `WANDB_API_KEY` in the environment before calling `weave.init()` [S2].

Based on the docs I read, no: `@weave.op` alone isn't the documented route to the Agents view. The agent-tracing guide treats Ops as a separate workflow and points you to "Trace LLM applications" for tracing individual functions with `@weave.op` [S1]. I did not find a page saying a bare `@weave.op` populates Agents conversations and turns, but I only searched this snapshot, so that isn't proof it can't happen.

- **Instrument the agent data model.** The Agents view models an agent, its conversations, the turns in each, the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions [S1]. To produce this yourself, use the agent tracing APIs. For example, `weave.start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on child spans so turns are grouped in the Agents tab [S5].
- **Or use a built-in integration.** Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own. Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation, and `weave.init()` alone isn't enough there [S3].
- **Where to look.** Instrumented traces appear in the **Agents** tab, where the Conversations tab lists conversations and the detail view shows turns, LLM calls, and tool executions [S2].

Minimal sketch, showing only the conversation step from the docs [S5]:

```python
conversation = weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent")
```

The docs I read don't specify how `@weave.op` calls interact with these conversations, so I can't say more about combining them.
